# Acast

- Category: host (plus monetization network)
- Checked: 2026-09-26
- Primary docs: https://www.acast.com/en, https://learn.acast.com/en/, https://developers.acast.com/

> **Verified 2026-09-26 (P0-03).** This file is the research-pass evidence for one vendor. Pricing, IAB certification and Apple HLS partner cells were rechecked against primary sources; corrections are marked inline. IAB status comes from the [IAB Tech Lab compliance registry](https://iabtechlab.com/compliance-programs/compliant-companies/). Apple's own partner search ([podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search](https://podcastsconnect.apple.com/partner-search)) redirects to an Apple ID sign-in, so partner status is attributed to the vendor or trade press, not an Apple list (checked 2026-09-26). The summary and comparison are in [`../vendors.md`](../vendors.md).

## Integration surface

- **API:** Acast Publishing API (REST) at `https://open.acast.com/<route>`, documented via developers.acast.com and the Learning Center article. Auth: `X-API-Key` header, key issued manually by Acast's customer success team (no public self-serve API key generation found). Rate limit: 60 requests/minute. Scope: shows/episodes CRUD, ad markers. Access is limited to the Pro and Video plans or Acast Creator Network ([pricing](https://www.acast.com/en/pricing), 2026-09-26). [Acast Publishing API | Learning Center](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/5790019-acast-publishing-api) (2026-09-26)
- **Webhooks:** Documented concept ("What is a Webhook?") supporting notifications for events such as new episode publication; full event catalog not found on public pages. [What is a WebHook?](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/3505461-what-is-a-webhook) (2026-09-26)
- **Export formats:** Analytics/Insights data exportable as CSV or XLS per dashboard tab; Revenue Dashboard exports as CSV (up to 4 report types). Feed migration relies on a 301-style redirect mechanism rather than a bulk media/RSS export tool; the redirect flow explicitly warns that listen/revenue history is lost once redirected, so historical analytics is not exportable after that point unless downloaded beforehand. [Data Exports: Getting set up](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/4165718-data-exports-getting-set-up) (2026-09-26; returned HTTP 401 on recheck, CSV export also shown in the Insights article); [Revenue Dashboard](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/4458070-revenue-dashboard) (2026-09-26); [How to redirect your podcast...](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/5087325-how-to-redirect-your-podcast-cancel-your-subscription-or-delete-your-account) (2026-09-26)
- **SSO / auth:** Undocumented — no SSO/SAML mentions found in Acast's public pricing, help center, or API docs pages checked.
- **Lock-in risks:** (1) API access itself is plan-gated (Pro, Video, or Creator Network) and key issuance is manual/non-self-service, adding friction to building automation early. (2) Feed redirect is one-directional and destructive to analytics history ("you will lose access once the redirect is in place") — there's no bulk historical-data export tied to the redirect flow, so a departing customer must proactively export CSVs beforehand. (3) Ads must be manually disabled by Acast support before a monetized show can be redirected/exported cleanly, creating a support-dependency step in any exit. (4) Acast+ Access private feeds are Acast-issued and fee-bearing per activation; migrating an existing private-feed subscriber base to a different platform is undocumented. [How to redirect your podcast...](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/5087325-how-to-redirect-your-podcast-cancel-your-subscription-or-delete-your-account) (2026-09-26); [Acast Publishing API | Learning Center](https://learn.acast.com/en/articles/5790019-acast-publishing-api) (2026-09-26); [Acast+ Access press release (third-party)](https://podnews.net/press-release/acast-plus-access) (2026-09-26)

## Narrative (≤150 words)

Acast covers most of Relay's checklist at the surface level — multi-show accounts, scoped user roles, video with a confirmed Apple Podcasts HLS partnership, on-demand AI transcripts with `podcast:transcript` RSS support, CSV/XLS analytics export, IAB Podcast Measurement certification, and private/premium feeds via Acast+ Access. It is weaker on Relay's specific needs: there's no documented editorial approval-before-publish workflow or immutable release record (only access-level roles), no dedicated comments/community feature, and the public Publishing API is plan-gated with manually-issued keys rather than self-service, limiting how deeply Relay could integrate without commercial negotiation. The biggest portability risk is the feed-redirect exit path: it is one-way, requires manual ad-teardown coordination with Acast support, and explicitly discards analytics/revenue history unless exported first — a meaningful contrast with Relay's goal of an open, portable, immutable record.

## Research notes

- `help.acast.com` did not resolve (DNS failure); Acast's help/support content actually lives at `learn.acast.com`, which was used instead.
- `developers.acast.com` loaded but WebFetch could not extract endpoint-level documentation content (likely rendered client-side or behind further navigation); endpoint/auth/rate-limit details were instead corroborated via the Learning Center article and third-party API cataloging (api-evangelist, apis.io) — flagged as lower-confidence secondary sourcing for the exact rate limit (60 req/min) and auth header format.
- The IAB Tech Lab certification PDF (compliance.iabtechnologylab.com, 12.06.2024 report) could not be text-extracted via WebFetch (binary/compressed PDF); the "v2.0" certification detail and 2019 "first certified" claim come from third-party press coverage (Inside Radio, Medium/Acast blog, Podcast Business Journal) rather than a directly parsed IAB document. Verification replaced this with the IAB registry entry: v2.2, 2026-02-18.
- Pricing page did not specify a numeric team-seat limit per plan, so the "3 staff seats" scenario element cannot be fully confirmed as covered by the Video plan — flagged as a gap rather than assumed.
- No explicit region/geography limits for Acast Marketplace eligibility were found on the pages checked; third-party listener-threshold figures (5,000 / 10,000 downloads for real revenue) are commentary, not vendor-published eligibility rules, and are labeled accordingly.
- No dedicated custom-feed-domain (as opposed to website domain) article was located.
